source: Oyserman & Lee (2008) Does culture influence what and how we think? Effects of priming individualism and collectivism. Psychological Bulletin 134(2)
finding: Meta-analysis of the culture-priming literature. Effects were moderate for relationality and cognition, small for self-concept and values. Robust across prime methods and consistent in direction and size with cross-national differences.
numbers: Abstract only read (Europe PMC). Counts from the chapter version: 67 studies, 5,818 participants (see a03).
quote: Effect sizes were moderate for relationality and cognition, small for self-concept and values
limits: Abstract only. Journal PDF blocked this session. Authors say unique effects of individualism versus honor or power cannot be told apart without primes for those.
agent_relevance: A cue can move a thinking style by a moderate amount in people. This is the human base rate for the idea that a cue switches the frame.

source: Oyserman (2007) Priming culture: culture as situated cognition, Handbook of Cultural Psychology ch.10 (summarises the Oyserman & Lee 2007/2008 meta-analysis)
finding: Oyserman's chapter lays out the situated-cognition account. Culture syndromes (individualism, collectivism) are knowledge structures. A cue makes one more accessible, and it then shapes content (values, self-concept, relations) and process (separate versus connected reasoning).
numbers: Reviews the 2007 meta-analysis search: 67 priming studies, 5,818 participants. Settings: US, Canada, Hong Kong, Singapore, Germany, Netherlands, Nepal, Philippines. Languages: English, German, Dutch, Chinese.
quote: culture is a conceptual prime, activating relevant knowledge
limits: Chapter, not the original paper. Authors call for primes in Latin America, Africa, the Middle East, and off college campuses.
agent_relevance: Gives a clean two-part model: priming of content and priming of procedure (mind-set). Our scaffold can ask which of the two a cue is meant to change.

source: Oyserman (2007) Priming culture: culture as situated cognition, Handbook of Cultural Psychology ch.10 (summarises the Oyserman & Lee 2007/2008 meta-analysis)
finding: Overall priming effect was small-to-moderate. It did not differ when Asian or Asian American samples were compared with European or European American samples.
numbers: Mean weighted d = 0.34; mean unweighted d = 0.45; 67 studies, N = 5,818. 36 studies in the US; 44 in English. Only about one third had gender in the design. 7 studies were cross-national replications.
limits: Most studies had no control condition. Those that did show small effects for individualism-vs-control and collectivism-vs-control. Mostly college students. Published English literature only; no publication-bias correction in this summary.
agent_relevance: Plan for d near 0.3, not a switch. Do not count on one cue to flip a style.

source: Oyserman (2007) Priming culture: culture as situated cognition, Handbook of Cultural Psychology ch.10 (summarises the Oyserman & Lee 2007/2008 meta-analysis)
finding: Effect size depends on the outcome. Cognition and relationality show the largest effects. Values and self-concept are small.
numbers: Studies per outcome: values k=15 (small), self-concept k=21 (small), relationality k=13 (moderate to large), cognition k=28 (moderate to large). Known value scales (Triandis, Schwartz) used as a validity check: moderate.
limits: Twenty Statements Test coding gave no effect for number of relational identities; trait coding may hide the real change.
agent_relevance: Style or procedure (cognition) moves more than stated self-view. For an agent, priming a way of processing may beat priming a stated value.

source: Oyserman (2007) Priming culture: culture as situated cognition, Handbook of Cultural Psychology ch.10 (summarises the Oyserman & Lee 2007/2008 meta-analysis)
finding: Prime type matters. Sumerian Warrior and SDFF give moderate effects on values, Pronoun Circling gives small ones. Language as a prime is weakest on values.
numbers: Task counts: Pronoun Circling n=15, Sumerian Warrior n=12, SDFF n=10, language n=10, scrambled sentence n=7, group imagination n=8, group instantiation n=3. Language prime on values weighted d = 0.10. On relationality SDFF and scrambled sentence large; Warrior and Pronoun Circling moderate. Mixed relational+collective primes moderate; single-level primes small.
limits: Task and outcome are confounded: SDFF mostly used for one outcome, Pronoun Circling for many. The authors say so.
agent_relevance: Cue strength depends on how close the cue is to the target task. Put the cue next to the task.

source: Oyserman (2007) Priming culture: culture as situated cognition, Handbook of Cultural Psychology ch.10 (summarises the Oyserman & Lee 2007/2008 meta-analysis)
finding: Trafimow, Triandis and Goto (1991) built the two classic primes. SDFF: think for 2 minutes about what makes you different from family and friends (individualism) or what you have in common (collectivism). Sumerian Warrior: read a story where a choice is justified by individual talent or by tribe and family.
numbers: Study 1 (SDFF) and Study 2 (Sumerian Warrior). The Warrior text was reused in 12 later studies, SDFF in 10.
limits: Original sample sizes and test statistics not seen; only the task descriptions in the chapter were read.
agent_relevance: The oldest cue form is a short thinking task, not a single word. Cheap to copy as a prompt prefix.

source: Oyserman (2007) Priming culture: culture as situated cognition, Handbook of Cultural Psychology ch.10 (summarises the Oyserman & Lee 2007/2008 meta-analysis)
finding: Pronoun Circling (Gardner, Gabriel and Lee 1999; logic from Brewer and Gardner 1996): circle I/me/my versus we/us/our in a short story about a city trip. The idea is to bring the concepts I and we to mind.
numbers: Used in 15 studies in the meta-analysis. Scrambled-sentence variants use words like separate, unique versus together, team, shared.
limits: Original N and effect not read here. Pronoun Circling gives only small average effects on values and self-concept.
agent_relevance: A trivial lexical cue is claimed to shift self-view. In LLMs the closest analogue is pronoun or persona framing in the prompt.

source: Oyserman (2007) Priming culture: culture as situated cognition, Handbook of Cultural Psychology ch.10 (summarises the Oyserman & Lee 2007/2008 meta-analysis)
finding: Procedural effects. Stapel and Koomen (2001): individualism priming led to contrast with a comparison target, collectivism priming to assimilation. Haberstroh et al. (2002): collectivism-primed Germans became as sensitive to conversational norms as unprimed Chinese.
numbers: Effect on cognition: moderate across tasks (group instantiation small).
limits: Second-hand in the chapter; original means and N not read.
agent_relevance: Priming moves how information is combined (contrast versus assimilate), not only what is said. Fits our interest in switching reasoning style.

source: Kuhnen & Oyserman (2002) Thinking about the self influences thinking in general: cognitive consequences of salient self-concept. J Exp Soc Psychol
finding: Priming independent versus interdependent self (pronoun task) changed context-sensitive processing and spatial memory: better recall of object locations in the interdependent condition.
numbers: Numbers not read. A later digital replication (a21) reproduced the direction.
limits: Known only via a search summary; DOI unverified; not opened.
agent_relevance: Early evidence that a self-frame cue shifts a general processing style.

source: Hong, Morris, Chiu & Benet-Martinez (2000) Multicultural minds: a dynamic constructivist approach to culture and cognition. American Psychologist 55(7)
finding: Theory: a cultural knowledge structure guides interpretation only if it is accessible (recent exposure) and applicable. Bicultural participants shown American or Chinese cultural icons switched their interpretive frame.
numbers: Abstract only read. Per search summary: more internal attributions after American cues, more external after Chinese cues. Sample sizes not read.
limits: Full text not opened. Biculturals may differ from monoculturals; this is the frame-switching base case.
agent_relevance: Gives the accessibility x applicability rule. A cue works only if the task matches the frame it activates.

source: Tao, Viberg, Baker & Kizilcec (2024) Cultural bias and cultural alignment of large language models. PNAS Nexus
finding: Five GPT models answered ten World Values Survey questions. Default answers sit near English-speaking and Protestant European countries. A cultural prompt (answer as an average human born in the country) moves answers closer for most countries.
numbers: 107 countries; ten prompt variants. Alignment improved for 71.0% (GPT-4o), 81.3% (GPT-4-turbo), 77.6% (GPT-4), 72.6% (GPT-3.5-turbo), 80.4% (GPT-3). Mean cultural distance fell 2.42 to 1.57 (GPT-4o), 2.71 to 1.77 (GPT-4-turbo), 2.69 to 1.65 (GPT-4); all P < 0.001.
quote: cultural prompting failed to improve cultural alignment or exacerbated cultural bias
limits: Fails or worsens in 19-29% of countries. GPT-4o: Finland 0.20 to 2.43, Luxembourg 0.59 to 2.72, Switzerland 0.45 to 2.48, Taiwan 2.40 to 3.94. Short survey answers only.
agent_relevance: Orientation cues work in LLMs on average but unevenly, and can overshoot where the default already fits. Check the shift against a measure.

source: Tao et al. (2024) Cultural bias and cultural alignment of LLMs (best case)
finding: Size of a cue effect when the default is far from the target: Jordan's gap to the survey fell from 4.10 to 0.36 with GPT-4o told to answer as a person from Jordan.
numbers: GPT-4o, Jordan: 4.10 to 0.36. Prompting in another language was reported ineffective in prior work on 14 countries.
limits: One model, one best-case country. Units are IVS cultural-map Euclidean distance.
agent_relevance: Cue effect is large when the default is far from the target and can be negative when it is near.

source: Cao, Zhou, Lee, Cabello, Chen & Hershcovich (2023) Assessing cross-cultural alignment between ChatGPT and human societies: an empirical study
finding: ChatGPT answered Hofstede VSM questions for US, CN, DE, JP, ES. Alignment is strongest for the US. English prompts shrink variance and pull answers toward American values. Prompting in the target language helps most cultures.
numbers: Spearman: US 0.70 (p 0.12) on prompt 1; CN -0.77 (p 0.07); ES prompts 1&2 combined 0.93 (p 0.01). Case: time for personal life for Japanese runs from utmost important (English prompt) to moderate (Japanese prompt). Injecting correct cultural knowledge scored 2.5 versus 1.5 original; anti-factual knowledge was accepted (score 1.0).
limits: Only five cultures, few dimensions, most p-values not significant. ChatGPT, early 2023.
agent_relevance: Cues by language and by injected cultural text both shift answers; wrong injected text is accepted too. Gate cue content.

source: Kharchenko, Roosta, Chadha & Shah (2025) How well do LLMs represent values across cultures? Empirical analysis based on Hofstede dimensions. KDD 2025
finding: Persona prompts for 36 countries, translated into 36 languages, on advice requests built from Hofstede dimensions. Models tell individualist from collectivist answers but do not follow them consistently.
numbers: Only one combination gave a significant correlation between country value and response: GPT-4o, individualism vs collectivism, high-resource languages plus multilingual approach, r = 0.71 (p < 0.05). Other cells: GPT-4 personas 0.38, multilingual 0.47; Command R+ multilingual -0.1. Japan and US have similar Hofstede individualism but models gave Japan collectivist and US individualist answers.
limits: 50 hand-written prompts; mid and low resource languages sometimes align better than high (GPT-4 uncertainty avoidance r = -0.656 in one cell).
agent_relevance: A persona cue does not give a calibrated orientation; models lean on stereotypes. A frame cue is not a controlled dial.

source: AlKhamissi & AlKhamissi et al. (2024) Investigating cultural alignment of large language models
finding: LLMs align better with a culture when prompted in its dominant language and when pretrained on its language mix. The paper proposes Anthropological Prompting (ask the model to take emic and etic views, context, background) to raise alignment.
numbers: Egypt survey, GPT-3.5, English prompts: vanilla persona prompting soft 0.4834 / hard 0.2443; anthropological prompting soft 0.5102 / hard 0.2838. Anthropological prompting needs 1 response per question versus 5 for vanilla.
limits: Single model and one survey for the headline comparison. Gains are modest (about +0.03 soft, +0.04 hard).
agent_relevance: A prompt that asks the model to reason about context beats a bare persona label. Candidate wording for a framing operator.

source: Lu, Song & Zhang (2025) Cultural tendencies in generative AI. Nature Human Behaviour
finding: GPT used in Chinese (vs English) shows more interdependent social orientation and more holistic cognitive style. ERNIE replicates it. Exploratory: cultural prompts (assume the role of a Chinese person) adjust these tendencies.
numbers: Abstract only (Europe PMC). Effect sizes not read.
limits: Full text not opened. The prompt result is exploratory. Challenged by the Sun and Wang replication.
agent_relevance: Closest LLM test of the claim that a cue shifts analytic versus holistic style. Treat as unreplicated.

source: Sun & Wang (2025) The fragility of cultural tendencies in LLMs (critical replication)
finding: Replication of Lu, Song and Zhang with 8 LLMs (4 US-based, 4 China-based) and more items. Prompt language had minimal effect. The framing instruction itself changed outputs far more.
numbers: Cultural-stability and entity-change task, 960 observations: prompt language mean diff 0.0053, p = 0.15, d = 0.045; Chinese-model advantage 0.021, p = 0.0089, d = 0.169; change-framed vs neutral prompts d = -2.095 (mean diff -0.165), eta-squared 0.5423. Only qwen had language d > 0.2 (d = 0.540). Two API prompt templates gave no significant difference. Temperature 0.
limits: A critique paper. Tasks differ from the original. The manipulation is prompt language, not an explicit orientation prime.
agent_relevance: A framing cue can swamp language or origin (d near 2). The cue effect is real, but culture here is context-sensitive pattern completion, not an inner trait.

source: Sun & Wang (2025) The fragility of cultural tendencies in LLMs (task-by-task)
finding: Across tasks, prompt language moved only gpt (two tasks) and ernie (one task). The other three English LLMs showed no effect in any experiment. The authors call the tendencies fragile artifacts of model and task.
numbers: Picture task: only ernie differed by language, no effect in 5 of 7 tasks. Interpersonal expectations: gpt better with Chinese prompts (p = 0.017); only kimi and gpt significant for language.
limits: Authors' own reading, one group, mid-2025 models.
agent_relevance: Failed-replication line for cueing LLM orientation by language. Do not rely on language alone as a cue.

source: Magid, Sarkol & Mesoudi (2017) Experimental priming of independent and interdependent activity does not affect culturally variable psychological processes. R Soc Open Sci 4:161025
finding: Two experiments tried to shift self-construal and analytic-holistic thinking with solitary versus collective activity (bandit vs public goods game; origami alone vs in a group). Only one of seven measures moved as predicted, in one experiment.
numbers: Experiment 1: 82 students after exclusions (41 per condition), 2x2 mixed pre/post design, 7 measures from 5 tasks. Cites the 67-study meta-analysis d = 0.34. Experiment 2 N not extracted.
quote: no convincing evidence that either solitary or collective tasks affected any of the measures
limits: Activity primes, not word primes. Authors say the tasks may be inadequate or the measures fixed early in life. The one significant effect (landscape objects, men) did not relate to condition.
agent_relevance: Boundary: behaviour-style primes did not shift style. A cue may need to be conceptual and next to the task.

source: Wu (2021) Self-construal priming does not shift self-descriptions, value endorsement, or social obligation judgment: a preregistered replication and extension (PsyArXiv)
finding: Preregistered replication of Gardner, Gabriel and Lee (1999) with Chinese participants using story primes and word-search (pronoun) primes. Priming did not change relative independence or interdependence. No moderation by gender, time abroad, rice versus wheat legacy, or earnestness.
numbers: Abstract only. Fails 3 preregistered criteria per a search summary. Sample sizes not read.
limits: Preprint, abstract only, one culture (China).
agent_relevance: Key failed direct replication of the best-known pronoun prime on self-construal measures. Lowers our prior on small lexical cues in humans.

source: Digital replication of Kuhnen & Oyserman (2002) spatial-memory self-construal priming (citation not confirmed)
finding: A digital replication reproduced better recall of objects in their original location in the interdependent versus independent condition. The effect was strongest when participants who did not comply with the pronoun task were excluded, and absent when they were included.
numbers: From a search summary only; numbers not read.
limits: Not opened. Authors and journal not confirmed. Compliance with the prime is the boundary condition.
agent_relevance: Check that the model actually followed the cue instruction before measuring its effect.

source: Liu, Liang, Feng & Zhou (2019) Self-construal priming affects holistic face processing and race categorization, but not face recognition. Front Psychol
finding: Mixed results for pronoun-circling priming of independent, interdependent and relational self on face tasks. Exp 1A: no priming effect. Exp 1B: independent priming gave less holistic processing. Exp 2: independent group showed a larger congruency effect than the relational group. No effect on face recognition.
numbers: Exp 1: control, interdependent, independent groups. Exp 2: four groups of about 21-22 participants. Exp 3: 80 participants kept after 3 lost to eye-tracker calibration.
limits: Small cells (about 21 per group), Chinese undergraduates. Some tasks show an effect, others none.
agent_relevance: Cue effects depend on the probe task. Expect a pattern of shows-up-on-some, absent-on-others.

source: Mishra & Bost (2018) Investigating the effects of cultural-mindset priming on evaluation of job performance behaviors (PMC6266528)
finding: Independent versus interdependent pronoun circling changed the weights raters put on behaviours in overall job judgments. Independent-primed raters gave less weight to citizenship behaviour and more to counterproductive behaviour. No change for task performance.
numbers: N = 174 US undergraduates, 87 per condition; 63% women; 67.3% Caucasian. Policy-capturing regression on vignettes.
limits: Students, role-play vignettes; test statistics not extracted; journal name not confirmed.
agent_relevance: Priming can move how evidence is weighted in a judgment, not only attitudes. Parallel to switching an evidence-weighting frame.

source: Jiang & Sui (2022) Bicultural minds: a cultural priming approach to the self-bias effect. Behav Sci
finding: Word-search (Exp 1, implicit) and reflective-thinking (Exp 2, explicit) primes were followed by perceptual matching. Interdependent priming reduced self-bias in people with low bias versus high bias in the neutral condition. Independent priming did not change self-bias. Replicated across both prime methods.
numbers: Experiment 1: 36 British Caucasian students (10 male, 26 female, mean age 22.22). Experiment 2 N not extracted.
limits: Very small sample. Asymmetry: only the interdependent prime worked, and only in a subgroup.
agent_relevance: One-sided priming effects are common. An agent cue may move one direction only.

source: Self-construal priming modulates self-evaluation under social threat (2017) Front Psychol
finding: In Chinese participants, independent priming gave a greater above-average effect under social-evaluative threat. The pattern disappeared after interdependent or neutral priming.
numbers: Abstract only (Experiment 2 combined priming with threat). Sample sizes not read.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: The cue changes behaviour only under threat. Cue effects are conditional on context.

source: Oyserman (2007) Priming culture: culture as situated cognition, Handbook of Cultural Psychology ch.10 (summarises the Oyserman & Lee 2007/2008 meta-analysis)
finding: Cross-national benchmark the priming effects are compared against. The Oyserman, Coon and Kemmelmeier (2002) meta-analysis found US-East Asia differences moderate but heterogeneous. US-China moderate to large; US-Korea and US-Japan small and scale-dependent; no difference among English-speaking countries.
numbers: 50 US-versus-other-country studies covering 64 countries; 35 within-US studies with 68 comparisons. Scale content (uniqueness versus competition items) changes the Asian American and African American gaps.
limits: Scale means, not behaviour. The East versus West split is weaker than usually stated.
agent_relevance: Warns against a single East-West dial for the agent. Orientation is a bundle of features.

source: Oyserman (2007) Priming culture: culture as situated cognition, Handbook of Cultural Psychology ch.10 (summarises the Oyserman & Lee 2007/2008 meta-analysis)
finding: Open problems the authors list. It is unclear which part of a prime carries the effect. English as a language prime could mean a foreign language, the colonizer's language or a second home language. Priming does not yet cover Latin America, Africa or the Middle East.
numbers: Language prime on values: weighted d = 0.10, no effect on value scales; 10 language-prime studies.
limits: Authors' discussion.
agent_relevance: In LLMs prompt language mixes several cues. Test language and explicit role separately.

source: Oyserman (2007) Priming culture: culture as situated cognition, Handbook of Cultural Psychology ch.10 (summarises the Oyserman & Lee 2007/2008 meta-analysis)
finding: No formal or computational model of orientation priming appeared in the sources read. The working model is verbal: semantic and procedural priming, with accessibility and applicability from Hong et al. (2000).
numbers: Zero formal models found among the sources opened.
limits: Search was limited. A spreading-activation or Bayesian model may exist elsewhere.
agent_relevance: We could build a small test: cue, then measure, with a compliance check, using accessibility x applicability as the design rule.
